angada.text: Duplicate `self.downsize` method definition overrides the 5-argument version, causing ArgumentError when Jobs::ResizeEmoji calls OptimizedImage.downsize with 5 arguments, breaking emoji resizing entirely

Client-side upload size check in validateUploadedFile is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using configured max_attachment_size_kb or max_image_size_kb settings, causing mismatch between client and server validation
Downsize loop in create_upload ignores the return value of OptimizedImage.downsize, causing failed conversions (like animated GIFs) to repeat 5 times unnecessarily
Downsize loop checks tempfile.size on a handle that may be stale after the file is rewritten, potentially allowing oversized uploads
API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB in create_upload regardless of site settings, silently capping sites with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB

Migration assumes legacy embed_category setting always has a matching category row - when no match exists, execute()[0]['id'] raises NoMethodError, aborting migration for fresh installations or when configured category was renamed/deleted

create_table with force: true drops embeddable_hosts if it already exists, destroying all host/category mappings on rerun after partial deployment or when table was created manually/by earlier version

When saving new host without choosing category, the save action sets host.category from local null categoryId instead of using server-returned category ID, causing row to show no category badge until page reload despite server storing Uncategorized
before_validation callback dereferences host before format validator can handle missing value - request without embeddable_host[:host] raises NoMethodError instead of validation error, returning 500
PUT for missing or deleted host reaches save_host(nil) which dereferences host.host, returning 500 instead of not-found response for stale admin requests

Migration copies existing embeddable_hosts setting entries verbatim including scheme (https://example.com), but record_for_host looks up only bare hostname, causing previously configured hosts to be rejected after migration

record_for_host lowercases only database column, not parsed host value - URI preserves case so referer with uppercase hostname doesn't match configured lowercase host despite DNS being case-insensitive
Model validation accepts hosts with port but URI#host removes port before lookup, so configured example.com:8080 can never match referer http://example.com:8080/
delete action doesn't handle rejected destroy promise with popupAjaxError like save action does - failed DELETE produces unhandled rejection with no user-facing error
_hydrateEmbedded removes *_ids field even when response doesn't include corresponding embedded collection, causing _lookupSubType to return undefined and original IDs to be lost
Legacy site setting is interpolated directly into SQL without quoting - apostrophe in configured host causes migration failure or SQL injection during upgrade

TopicsController#unsubscribe assumes a TopicUser row exists, but TopicView.new only loads/authorizes the topic and does not create one. A logged-in user can follow this route for any visible topic they have never visited, leaving tu nil and raising NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing.

The unsubscribe action performs state-changing operations via GET request. Mail clients and security scanners commonly prefetch GET links, so merely opening/scanning the email can change the recipient's topic notification setting without user action.

TopicsController#unsubscribe bypasses TopicUser.change which is the normal notification-level update path. This means notifications_changed_at and user_changed reason are not set, and the /topic/:id notification-level change is not published on MessageBus, leaving other open topic views with stale state.
Stored XSS vulnerability at app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19
SSRF vulnerability at app/models/topic_embed.rb:46
Flex .small-action shrink-wraps .small-action-desc because .small-action-desc has no flex: 1 or width, causing floated edit/delete buttons to sit next to text instead of at the right edge of the row

Padding change on .small-action-desc from 4em left padding to 0 1.5% leaves the mobile .custom-message negative margin (-40px) stale, causing the message to be pulled left and potentially overlap the avatar or clip

Removing float: right from .panel breaks alignment in server-rendered header because the .row wrapper is not a flex container, so margin-left: auto and order(3) do not position the login panel correctly

`website_name` is not included in `untrusted_attributes`, so a TL0 user viewed anonymously can receive this derived value even though the existing `website` field is intentionally suppressed, bypassing the privacy restriction and exposing the user's website to anonymous viewers

The domain comparison treats any two hosts with the same number of labels as sharing the same domain after dropping the first label (e.g., `evil.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`), incorrectly treating unrelated domains as the same site due to lack of public-suffix-aware checking

The conditional serializer hook is named `include_website_name` but ActiveModel Serializers 0.8 looks for `include_website_name?` (with trailing question mark), so the hook is ignored and `website_name` is serialized as nil for users with no website
`.custom-message-length` branches are swapped in mobile/modal.scss - light theme uses $primary at 30% instead of original 70%, making character-count hint dark and prominent instead of subdued
`.topic-meta-data h5 a` in desktop/topic-post.scss uses $primary at 70% for light branch instead of original 30%, making reply-author links much paler and lowering contrast
`.group-member-info .name` in desktop/user.scss uses $primary at 50% for light branch instead of original 30%, causing group member names to lose visual hierarchy by matching .title colour
`.group-member-info .name` in mobile/user.scss uses $primary at 50% for light branch instead of original 30%, causing mobile group member names to lose emphasis and match .title shade
Topic-map `h3` in mobile/topic-post.scss uses $primary at 50% for light branch instead of original 20%, making heading lighter and matching h4 below it, reducing contrast
Math.floor(count / limit) + 1 reports an extra page whenever count is an exact multiple of limit (for example, 50 members yields 2 pages), causing the UI to display an empty second page

When a visible group has more than 50 members, findMembers requests only the first page and the public group.members template has no pagination or subsequent fetch, so members after the first 50 are silently omitted from the public group page

The new 50-row default limit applies to the public /groups/:name/members endpoint as well as the admin caller, causing non-automatic groups with more than 50 users to silently display only the first 50 with no way for users to reach the rest

When a member is removed from the final page, findMembers clamps offset using the pre-mutation user_count, so a group with 51 members viewed at offset 50 requests offset 50 after removal even though the new total is 50 and renders an empty page

Group#add calls self.users.push(user) which writes the join row immediately before save runs, so if the subsequent group validation/save fails, the action returns an error even though the member has already been added (non-atomic membership update)

remove_member deletes via the through-association by raw id and gives no feedback when the user is not a member - a user_id that is not a member raises RecordNotFound returning a 404 instead of silent success

Negative limit or offset values are passed directly to ActiveRecord without validation, causing PostgreSQL to reject negative LIMIT/OFFSET and return a 500 error instead of a valid or client-error response

Group#add calls users.push which attempts to insert a new group_users row, but the database has a unique (group_id, user_id) index, so adding an already-member user raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique and returns a 500 instead of being idempotent
Unbounded client-controlled limit on public endpoint allows oversized limit to serialize the whole group in one response
create action ignores alias_level parameter which the client sends, saving the new group with the default alias level regardless of the combo box choice
Test exercises remove_member with PUT even though the new route exposes this action as DELETE, so the test passes without validating the real route

Fallback locales are only preloaded in controller requests - when translations run outside a controller request (Sidekiq jobs, mailers using I18n.with_locale), I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is never called, causing fallback locales like :en to be unloaded and missing keys return 'translation missing' instead of fallback text

Fallback chain depends on mutable site setting but translate cache ignores it - when admin changes SiteSetting.default_locale, FallbackLocaleList#[] returns different fallback chain, but cached translations keyed only by key/locale/backend keep old fallback text until restart or reload

Call to nonexistent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation - UsernameForm.authenticate evaluates !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() but the only declaration is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user), so the services module fails to compile

isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so the initial login page loses passkeys - when evaluated for an unidentified user it returns false, causing authenticate and challenge to skip WebAuthn setup on normal first login and the conditional passkey form may not render

Test catches generic Exception instead of Selenium's expected missing-element exception - reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey catches Exception and treats it as expected absence of webauthn form, swallowing driver or page-load failures so negative assertions can pass without verifying intended behavior
Negative offset slice is passed to a Django queryset when enable_advanced_features is true and a client sends a cursor with a negative offset, causing the audit-log request to fail with a 500 error

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to AuditLogEntry.datetime which is a datetime object, raising TypeError and returning a 500 error when optimized_pagination=true is used on the audit log endpoint
value_from_cursor returns the raw integer instead of a datetime, so later pages would compare the datetime column to a number
BasePaginator.get_result clamps non-prev cursor negative offsets with max(0, offset) but the is_prev branch still slices with the raw negative offset, creating inconsistent behavior
Cursors built after offset clamping still use the unclamped cursor.offset value
Undocumented optimized_pagination flag exposes an experimental paginator that cannot handle datetime ordering key, turning a working endpoint into a 500 for superusers or global-access members
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key applies math.floor/math.ceil to datetime values instead of converting to epoch milliseconds first, causing TypeError
OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes negative cursor offsets directly to Django QuerySet slice, causing ValueError since Django doesn't support negative indexing
OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access when member can be None, causing AttributeError
BasePaginator.get_result passes negative cursor offsets to Django QuerySet slice, causing ValueError
zunionstore in add-buffer.lua uses default SUM aggregate instead of MIN, causing duplicate span scores to be doubled and breaking eviction order
Redirect-chain loop limit reduced from 10000 to 1000, causing incomplete segment merging for deep redirect chains

Top-level Git submodule entry pointing at an unrelated commit without .gitmodules declaration - sentry-repo is a mode-160000 gitlink to commit a5d290951 that cannot be fetched and breaks submodule operations

_is_error_focused_query returns true from raw substring match when query contains !event.type:error or combines event.type:error with another event type, causing incorrect count() to upsampled_count() replacement for non-error rows
transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling leaves nested count() unchanged in equation expressions like equation|count() / 100, causing inconsistent results between plain count() and equations

When top_events > 0 and upsampling is enabled, final_columns only changes timeseries query while top events are still selected and ranked by raw count(), potentially returning weighted series for wrong top-N groups

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects uses outer dataset and request query instead of scoped_dataset or rewritten query, causing transaction-only split queries to be incorrectly rewritten to upsampled_count()
upsampled_count() SnQL function is publicly exposed and emits sum(sample_weight) even for transactions or non-allowlisted data without sample_weight column, causing Snuba query failures

Cached allowlist decision from is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects goes stale for up to 60 seconds when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist option changes, and invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called
upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without a default - sum() skips NULLs so events with NULL sample_weight contribute 0 instead of 1, causing undercounting
_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling writes sample_rate unconditionally for truthy out-of-range or non-numeric client_sample_rate values, allowing invalid sampling weights like 1.5 to be stored
Table widget renders hard-coded empty data when use-table-widget-visualization feature flag is enabled - tableResultComponent passes empty columns and tableData instead of actual query results
useFeedbackSummary reads data.summary and data.numFeedbacksUsed without guarding for undefined data when query is disabled, causing potential crash on feedback page
fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() by position, causing wrong error attribution when some events are missing from nodestore
Attributes component returns sorted list before applying HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter when search query is empty, showing is_segment, project_id, and received attributes
TraceTabsAndVitals uses Flex without gap prop, losing the 8px spacing that was provided by the removed Container/FlexBox styles
BrowserReportSerializer accepts reports with neither age nor timestamp, or with zero values for one field alongside the other, due to truthiness checks instead of proper validation
test_mixed_fields doesn't cover edge case where age=0 and timestamp=0 are both present, which would pass validation incorrectly
drain_mailbox_parallel has 120 second taskworker deadline but loop runs until BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET (3 minutes), causing potential mid-batch interruption
gen_request_data compares rrweb millisecond timestamps with Sentry event timestamps in seconds, causing incorrect chronological ordering
get_environment_info performs separate Group.get_recommended_event Snuba lookup for each issue, causing up to 1000 extra queries for merged PRs
BrowserReportSerializer accepts negative age values since IntegerField lacks min_value constraint unlike timestamp field
process_raw_response removes error_ids when field parameters omit it, causing get to silently skip error context
TimeSince hidden-xs hidden-sm class is on inner element but TextOverflow wrapper remains visible, taking layout space on small viewports
makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions omits selection.environments, returning attribute keys from outside selected environment
useTraceItemAttributeKeys queryKey lacks organization.slug, causing cache reuse across organization switches
useTraceItemAttributeKeys uses useQuery without retry setting, causing default retry behavior instead of disabled retries like useApiQuery
AiContent shows project-not-found error when ProjectsStore hasn't finished loading instead of loading state
GroupingVariant no longer renders Type row for fallback/checksum variants with null description, making variant identification ambiguous
TabularColumn constrains name property to TFields generic, preventing custom display labels in typed tables
renderDefaultHeadCell and renderDefaultBodyCell use truthiness check for custom renderer return value, treating falsy values like 0 or '' as absent

When two concurrent authorize calls use the same valid backup code, both read the same encrypted list, pass indexOf, and overwrite the row with an otherwise identical list containing that code as null, so the same single-use code authenticates twice. Consume the code atomically with a conditional update or transaction and reject a stale write.

When the dialog is dismissed through Escape, the overlay, or the close button, onOpenChange only closes the parent and EnableTwoFactorModal preserves step and the generated codes, so reopening can land directly on the backup-code screen and expose the previous setup. Reset the setup state from the close path and clear the sensitive values before allowing the modal to reopen.

When navigator.clipboard.writeText is unavailable or rejects, this handler still calls showToast with a success message and leaves the promise unhandled, so users can believe their backup codes were copied when they were not. Await the clipboard operation and show success only after it resolves, with a caught failure message or fallback.

missing_backup_codes message points to a regeneration flow that does not exist - when a user who enabled 2FA before this change has a null backupCodes column, the message tells them to generate them in your settings but the diff adds no regeneration UI or endpoint, and setup.ts rejects already-enabled users, so a user without their authenticator is stuck.

When the disable dialog is dismissed while twoFactorLostAccess is enabled, the component remains mounted and this state is not reset, so reopening the dialog starts in backup-code mode with the previous form state rather than the normal TOTP flow. Reset the access mode and form when handling onOpenChange/cancel dismissal.

When a keyboard user tabs through a form containing PasswordField, the visibility button is removed from the tab sequence due to tabIndex={-1}, so that user cannot reveal or hide the password without using a pointer. This violates the keyboard-operability contract for the exposed button control.

When apps/web/components/security/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx calls TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable(password, totpCode) without a third argument, this required backupCode parameter makes the existing caller fail TypeScript compilation, so the build cannot type-check after this change. Make backupCode optional or update every caller.

Unguarded property access on possibly undefined main host destination calendar - when a booking uses MeetLocationType and evt.destinationCalendar is null, undefined or empty, create in packages/core/EventManager.ts dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration on an undefined value, throwing a TypeError before the Cal Video fallback

Booking references lose credentialId for video results and externalCalendarId for legacy calendar results - when results are mapped to booking references, create in packages/core/EventManager.ts sets credentialId to undefined for non-calendar (video) results, and calendar results from the credential-less branch carry no externalId

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition in organization creation - createHandler in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts now applies slug and requestedSlug the opposite way from before, with billing enabled the org gets its slug before payment, with billing disabled it keeps only a requestedSlug in metadata and no real slug

When a collective booking's first destination belongs to another integration (for example Google) and a later destination is CalDAV, BaseCalendarService.createEvent uses that first destination to filter this service's calendars, so it uploads to no CalDAV calendar while still returning a successful UID, silently omitting the later host's event

When a booking has multiple credential-backed destinations and the current credential is not the first destination, CalendarManager.createEvent discards externalId and CalendarService.createEvent receives only the credential ID, so adapters such as the base CalDAV service select calEvent.destinationCalendar[0] and write the event to the first host's calendar instead of the current host's calendar

When rescheduling with newBookingId and the old booking has multiple calendar references, updateAllCalendarEvents updates every reference but the merge cleanup still uses booking.references.find, so only the first old calendar event is deleted and the remaining events stay visible as stale duplicates

Fallback lookup in updateEvent compares externalId against an empty externalCalendarId - when updateEvent in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts is called without externalCalendarId, the fallback find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) compares against a falsy value and yields undefined, causing the Google update to fail

When a collective event has no eventType.destinationCalendar and no organizer calendar but a team host has a calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is null, so the optional push discards teamDestinationCalendars and createAllCalendarEvents creates no host event

loadUsers drops the organization select and turns an empty dynamic list into a 500 - when a dynamic-group booking has no eventTypeId, loadUsers in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts drops the organization select from the user query and throws a plain Error for an empty dynamicUserList which the catch block turns into a 500

createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId - when a destination calendar has no credentialId, createEvent in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts finds no entry matching the credential and inserts the event into primary instead of the configured destination's externalId

When a collective booking is confirmed through either Stripe payment path, getBooking/handlePaymentSuccess rebuilds evt.destinationCalendar from only the booking or organizer calendar, so EventManager.create schedules no event for the other collective hosts

When EventManager creates events for multiple destinations, LarkCalendarService.createEvent reads only the first array entry, so the second Lark host's event is posted to the first host's calendar (or fails with the wrong calendar)

Recurring bulk-delete block runs once per calendar reference - when a recurring booking with allRemainingBookings has several calendar references, handler in packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts reruns the whole credential-by-booking delete matrix once per reference, causing duplicated deletions and potentially pairing a uid with the wrong credential

updateEvent is called with an undefined credential when the DB lookup finds nothing - when a calendar reference's credentialId is found neither in memory nor in the database, updateAllCalendarEvents in packages/core/EventManager.ts still calls updateEvent with an undefined credential, causing the call to reject and return failure results for every reference

When no destination calendar matches credentialId and Google returns a hangoutLink, createEvent inserts into primary but the later calendar.events.patch uses the undefined selectedCalendar, so the description update is sent to an invalid calendar and its rejected promise is not handled

When a destination has an externalId but no credentialId, createAllCalendarEvents enters the credential-by-type branch and calls createEvent without destination.externalId, so GoogleCalendarService cannot select that destination and inserts on primary instead

When a recurring booking reference has a credentialId that is absent from bookingToDelete.user.credentials, the Prisma-loaded calendarCredential is used only to enter the branch, while the deletion matrix still iterates the in-memory credentials, so that credential's recurring events remain on the external calendar after cancellation

When app credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the native fetch Response without parsing its body, so Google, HubSpot and Zoho callers that expect parsed token objects fail when accessing res.data or token.access_token

minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.string().toString() which produces the literal string '[object Object]' instead of a wildcard key, causing expiry fields like expires_in or expiry_date to be stripped by Zod validation

In zoho-bigin CalendarService, credentialId is passed as the userId argument to refreshOAuthTokens, causing the sync endpoint to receive the wrong identifier and potentially return another user's tokens

zoho-bigin CalendarService treats the refreshOAuthTokens result as an Axios response and reads tokenInfo.data, but when credential sharing is enabled it receives a fetch Response, causing tokenInfo.data.error to throw

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns Zod's { success, data } safe-parse wrapper, but Google CalendarService stores this directly as credential.key, causing subsequent googleCredentialSchema.parse to fail
Salesforce getClient persists accessTokenParsed.data but constructs the jsforce.Connection with the old credentialKey.access_token, causing the first API operation to use the expired token
Salesforce CalendarService references prisma without importing it, causing TypeScript compilation failure or ReferenceError at runtime
Salesforce getClient refreshes the token on every construction without an expiry check and without going through refreshOAuthTokens, bypassing the credential-sync endpoint

When credential sharing is enabled, Lark CalendarService passes the sync endpoint's generic response to handleLarkError which expects the Lark envelope structure with data.data fields, causing refresh to fail
Webhook secret in app-credential.ts is compared using non-constant-time !== operator, potentially leaking timing information about the shared secret
salesforceTokenSchema requires a scope field but Salesforce's documented refresh response doesn't include it, causing parseRefreshTokenResponse to reject valid responses
minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed key [z.string().toString()] is a fixed literal string rather than an arbitrary numeric field, causing valid sync responses to fail Zoom refresh validation
Salesforce fetch has no timeout or cancellation, causing SalesforceCalendarService construction to hang indefinitely if the token endpoint stops responding
Office365 video refreshAccessToken saves the sync response directly as credential.key, overwriting the stored refresh_token and breaking future refreshes when sharing is disabled
Webex VideoApiAdapter validates sync response against webexRefreshedTokenSchema which requires refresh_token and refresh_token_expires_in that the sync response doesn't carry
app-credential.ts handler doesn't check req.method, allowing PUT, PATCH, or DELETE requests to mutate credentials instead of returning 405
Office365 video refreshAccessToken recomputes expiry_date from expires_in, but sync response doesn't carry expires_in, resulting in NaN expiry
Salesforce getClient checks response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok, rejecting valid responses with empty or non-OK reason phrases
Zoom VideoApiAdapter computes expiry_date from newTokens.expires_in, but when sync endpoint returns expiry_date instead, the result is NaN causing the token to never refresh
parseRefreshTokenResponse sets refresh_token to the literal string 'refresh_token' when omitted, even when credential sharing is disabled, potentially overwriting valid refresh tokens
app-credential.ts handler stores decrypted JSON directly without validating its shape against the app's credential contract, allowing invalid payloads like {} to overwrite working credentials
refreshOAuthTokens fetch has no timeout or abort signal, causing token refreshes to hang indefinitely if the credential-sync endpoint stalls
Office365 calendar refreshAccessToken removed previous logging of Zod errors and response body, losing diagnostics and leaving tokenResponse.success check as dead code
app-credential.ts handler has a race condition where concurrent requests for the same userId and appSlug can both observe no credential and create duplicates

When a calendar update fails, addGuestsHandler still returns success and sends the add-guest emails because EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents catches integration errors and returns failed results instead of throwing. The attendee rows are already committed, so the booking and external calendar diverge while users are told the guests were added.

EventManager is built with the acting user's credentials, not the organizer's. When a team admin or attendee adds guests, the organizer's external calendar event may not be updated, or a same-type calendar belonging to the caller is used instead.

When an accepted team administrator who is not an owner adds guests, isTeamAdminOrOwner requires both membership checks (isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner), so the administrator is rejected with FORBIDDEN even though isTeamAdmin explicitly accepts the ADMIN role.

When guests contains an existing attendee or a blacklisted address alongside a valid address, sendAddGuestsEmails receives the unfiltered input, so an existing attendee is classified as newly scheduled and the organizer notification describes rejected addresses as added.

When the add-guests mutation succeeds, addGuestsMutation closes the dialog and starts utils.viewer.bookings.invalidate() without awaiting or handling its promise, so a rejected invalidation becomes an unhandled rejection and the bookings list can remain stale.

Guest dedup and blacklist check are case-sensitive and ignore duplicates within the input. Blacklisted addresses bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, and existing attendees get re-added as duplicates when casing differs.

When a request contains the same email more than once, ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts both values and addGuestsHandler's uniqueGuests filter only checks existing attendees, so createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate guest notifications.

handleAdd does not guard against empty entries, and the error state is never cleared. The error message stays visible after the user corrects the emails, after a successful add, and when the dialog is dismissed another way.

When a user submits the same address with different casing, ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts both values because Set compares the raw strings case-sensitively, so addGuestsMutation sends both to the handler and createMany stores duplicate attendees.

No booking state validation before adding guests. When a booking is cancelled, rejected or already past, addGuestsHandler still inserts attendees and updates the calendar. Guests then receive a scheduled invite for an event that no longer applies.

When two requests concurrently add the same email to one booking, both can pass the in-memory filter because neither sees the other's uncommitted attendee, and Attendee has no unique constraint on (bookingId, email). createMany then inserts duplicate attendee rows.
No limit on the guests array. When an authorized caller submits a very large guests array, ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts it without a size bound, enabling spam or heavy load.
deleteMany in scheduleSMSReminders can delete non-SMS workflow reminders (email or WhatsApp) when they have retryCount greater than 1, because the second OR branch has no method filter

When isLockedForSMSSending is true, scheduleSMS returns undefined and the else branch increments retryCount as if delivery failed, causing reminders to be deleted after two cron runs without ever being sent

When an SMS reminder has no generated message or sendTo value, the retry logic never runs because both the provider call and catch block are bypassed, leaving the unscheduled row eligible on every cron run indefinitely
prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can throw and abort the whole cron run, skipping remaining reminders in unscheduledReminders

When workflowReminder.update that records scheduled: true throws after twilio.scheduleSMS has returned a SID, the catch block increments retryCount without recording the SID, causing duplicate SMS scheduling on next cron run
Transient failures from twilio.scheduleSMS consume the retry budget and permanently delete reminders after only two cron runs, same as permanent failures

When an org-scoped query reaches this condition, PostgreSQL receives teamIds as one bound JavaScript array parameter inside ANY, so Prisma's raw-query parameter serialization does not produce the typed integer[] expression required here and the query fails instead of enforcing authorization. The same construction is used for uniqueUserIds and userIdsFromTeam. Build a typed array with Prisma.join (or an explicit cast) inside ARRAY[...].

getBaseConditions can return an unparenthesized top-level OR. When only authorization conditions exist, getBaseConditions returns the auth Sql unwrapped, and the org and team builders return a bare (A) OR (B). A caller composing WHERE x AND ${baseConditions} gets x AND A OR B, so the OR branch skips the other predicates and can return bookings outside the intended date range or scope.
sed -i '' syntax is BSD/macOS specific and fails on GNU/Linux, causing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL replacement to fail silently while still printing success message

deleteCacheMutation in CredentialActionsDropdown only shows toast when onSuccess is omitted, never invalidating viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache timestamp and allowing repeated delete requests
cleanup function in test-gcal-webhooks.sh unconditionally exits with status 0, masking failures in tunnel initialization, URL extraction, rate-limit, and configuration
Tunnel identification uses broad command-line match for 'tmole 3000' which can match unrelated processes, and URL lookup uses potentially stale /tmp/tmole.log from another process
Cache deletion action remains available in CredentialActionsDropdown when disableConnectionModification is true or credential is delegation credential
ENV_FILE path '../.env' is resolved relative to caller's current directory instead of script's directory, potentially creating/updating wrong .env file
Fixed shared path /tmp/tmole.log has race condition between rm -f and shell redirection where another process could plant a symlink, and concurrent runs share logs
dev:cron script uses npx tsx but tsx is not declared as a dependency in package.json, may download unpinned version or fail offline
updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data relies on implicit @updatedAt bump by Prisma and touches calendars that were not actually refreshed

When immediateDelete is true (reschedule, workflow delete, step delete), deleteScheduledEmailReminder only POSTs the SendGrid cancel and returns. If that request fails, the catch just logs and cancelled is never set. The cron has nothing to retry, so the old email is still sent.

When the SendGrid cancel fails during workflow deletion, deleteScheduledEmailReminder catches and logs the error, and workflowsRouter.delete still deletes the workflow. The reminder rows are removed with it, so no retry record exists and the scheduled email is delivered.

When a booking is cancelled or rescheduled, handler in handleCancelBooking.ts calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without awaiting them. The response can return before the reminder is marked cancelled or deleted, and a serverless runtime can freeze first.

When one client.request cancel call throws for a reminder (invalid batch_id, 4xx, or 429), handler in scheduleEmailReminders.ts exits the whole loop. The DB deletes are only awaited after the loop, so no rows are removed and later cancelled reminders are skipped. The failing row is retried first each run, blocking the rest.

When a cancelled reminder's scheduledDate is already past at cron start, handler removes it in the earlier past-due deleteMany before the cancelled: true query runs. No SendGrid cancel is issued for that row, so a still-queued email can be delivered.

async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it may already have been awaited - forEach does not wait for async callbacks, so Promise.all(apiDeletes) can run while the array is still empty, leaving calendar events undeleted or failing unobserved

In wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts, bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not await the callback's getCalendar, deleteEvent or deleteMeeting promises, causing failures to bypass try/catch as unhandled rejections and email to be sent before deletions complete

In vital/lib/reschedule.ts, async forEach callback creates floating promises that forEach discards, causing rejections from getCalendar, deleteEvent or deleteMeeting to bypass try/catch and become unhandled

In bookings.tsx request-reschedule mutation, forEach(async ...) starts calendar and video deletions that nothing awaits, returning success while old events may still exist and rejections go unobserved

In packages/app-store/index.ts, appStore starts every import() immediately at module load instead of deferring until requested, causing all app modules to load at startup and failing imports for unused apps to become unhandled promise rejections
Working-hours check computes `end` from the slot start, so the end bound is never enforced - slots running past the cutoff are offered
`workingHours.find` rejects a slot that is valid under another working-hours entry - valid afternoon slots vanish when host has multiple working-hour ranges on same weekday
Dayjs objects compared with `===`, so the zero-length-override branch is dead - object identity is always false

When an override crosses the organizer/invitee calendar-day boundary, `activeOverrides` was selected using the raw UTC start against `startOfInviteeDay` before offset conversion - invitees see the override on the wrong day or not at all
Override upper bound tests the slot start instead of the slot end - slots starting before override ends but running past it are incorrectly offered

When one host has a date override on a day and another host does not, `checkIfIsAvailable` evaluates the flattened `dateOverrides` list without filtering by host - second host is treated as available for first host's override window

When an override falls on a DST transition, `getSlots` computes both offsets from the serialized UTC wall-clock value rather than the override's organizer-local date and time - override window can be shifted by an hour

When an override spans a daylight-saving transition, `getSlots` uses the offset calculated at `override.start` for both boundaries - converted end boundary is wrong and can expose or hide an hour of availability

Override offset depends on an optional `timeZone` and a locale-formatted date string - calling `.tz(override.timeZone)` with `undefined` falls back to process default zone, and parsing `override.start.toString()` drops milliseconds
Override matched by UTC calendar day of the slot with an inverted offset - override can fail to match, leaving host judged by normal working hours
Unguarded integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] raises KeyError when an existing active unlinked Integration has no sender in its metadata, causing a 500 error instead of the error page

When the OAuth callback includes a different installation_id, OAuthLoginView overwrites the installation selected before authorization, allowing the authenticated GitHub user to be paired with an installation other than the one that started the flow
In test_installation_not_found, the second self.client.get overwrites the response from the installation-ID request, so the test no longer verifies the missing-installation error handling

When GitHub rejects the authorization code or the token endpoint is unavailable, OAuthLoginView.dispatch lets safe_urlopen or get_user_info raise outside any try block, returning an unhandled 500 instead of a controlled error dialog
OAuth state compared with non-constant-time != operator instead of constant_time_compare
Redirect URL built without URL encoding for state and redirect_uri parameters

The `queued` default value in AssignmentSource is evaluated once at module import time using timezone.now(), causing all AssignmentSource instances created without an explicit queued value in long-lived processes to share the same stale timestamp

MetricAlertDetectorHandler subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only pass, leaving abstract hooks unimplemented, causing TypeError on instantiation and crashing process_detectors for metric_alert_fire detector type

build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts value parameter but never uses it, allowing tests to pass incorrect values (6 instead of 10, 100, or 8) without detecting regressions in build_occurrence_and_event_data
TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe calls build_mock_occurrence_and_event with group key 'val1' but DetectorEvaluationResult uses 'group_key', causing fingerprint mismatch in equality assertion

When two workers process failed check-ins for the same environment concurrently, both can read monitor_env.status as OK, independently evaluate the threshold, and enter the branch before either status save is visible, causing try_incident_threshold to emit duplicate occurrences for the same threshold window and potentially publish duplicate failure transitions. Need to serialize on the environment or use an atomic conditional transition before creating occurrences.

get_monitor_environment_context copies the config and replaces schedule_type with its display string, but then returns monitor_environment.monitor.config instead of the modified copy, so the occurrence's monitor context carries the raw schedule-type value and the copy/replacement have no effect.

When failed_checkins contains only statuses outside HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP (such as UNKNOWN or IN_PROGRESS values), get_failure_reason builds an empty human_status and returns ' check-ins detected' with no count or status, resulting in malformed incident evidence. Need to add an explicit fallback for empty status_counts or reject unsupported statuses before formatting.

Hung flusher processes are never killed because the isinstance check never matches SpawnProcess - when a flusher process hangs, _ensure_processes_alive only kills it if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is never true for spawn-context SpawnProcess objects, causing the hung process to keep running while a replacement is started on the same shards, which can duplicate flushes and leak processes

When produce_to_pipe is set and a worker thread exceeds max_unhealthy_seconds, _ensure_processes_alive starts a replacement without stopping the original thread, so both SpanFlusher.main loops flush the same Redis shards and publish duplicate payloads to Kafka - need cooperative cancellation for the old thread and wait for it to stop before creating the replacement

When the consumer is started with --flusher-processes -1, SpanFlusher computes num_processes = -1, creates no process entries, and then indexes the empty map while assigning shards, so startup fails with a KeyError; 0 is also silently treated as 'all shards' by the or fallback - need to validate this option as a positive integer before constructing the strategy

When a caller omits flusher_processes, ProcessSpansStrategyFactory passes None to SpanFlusher, whose max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) expands the default to one worker per assigned shard instead of the documented/default one worker, causing direct factory callers with multiple partitions to create multiple workers and multiply Redis/Kafka resource usage

When Arroyo creates more than one partition strategy from this factory, each strategy shares the queue_pool, but SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close shuts that pool down rather than only closing its own commit loop. Closing one revoked/finished partition stops workers used by every other partition strategy, leaving their queued messages unprocessed and offsets uncommitted.

When grouping_fn or queue_pool.submit raises for a decoded message, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit marks that Kafka offset complete, so the record is committed even though no worker processed it, silently dropping valid results on transient queue failures or grouping bugs.

When result_processor fails, OrderedQueueWorker.run logs the exception and then marks the record complete, so _commit_loop commits its offset and Kafka will not replay the failed result, contradicting the docstring that offsets are committed only after successful processing.

When FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown = True and then calls Queue.shutdown(immediate=False), a worker that finishes its current item exits at the while not self.shutdown check without draining already queued items, discarding queued Kafka records before they are processed.

test_preserves_order_within_group only checks the count and every decoded result has the same subscription_id/data, so it does not verify its ordering contract when SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy dispatches same-group messages out of order.

test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling accepts an empty commit map when the first message fails and the second succeeds, so a consumer that processes neither message for commit purposes passes despite the test claiming successful messages continue.

FixedQueuePool uses unbounded queues, so when Kafka delivers faster than the workers process results, SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit keeps accepting records instead of applying the documented backpressure and the process can accumulate an unbounded backlog in memory.

test_concurrent_processing_different_groups still passes when the queue pool runs all workers serially because the processor only appends results and the test waits for completion before checking the final count, not verifying actual concurrent execution.

test_thread_queue_parallel_concurrent_subscriptions still only waits for both callbacks and passes when FixedQueuePool is changed to route both groups through one worker, so it does not test the concurrency contract stated by its name.

SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy docstring claims backpressure and commit-after-success, but the code provides neither: queues are unbounded, poll() only emits a gauge, and failed items are still committed.
test_stats_reporting sees total_items == 0 and fails when the workers dequeue all ten items before the stats read, causing scheduling-dependent CI flakiness.

test_thread_queue_parallel_graceful_shutdown only checks that the pool reference is cleared when factory.shutdown() is called with queued work, so shutdown can stop workers and discard all five messages while still passing.

Any gap in observed offsets (transaction marker or compacted record) stalls commits for the partition permanently because OffsetTracker.get_committable_offsets stops scanning at that gap, causing all_offsets to grow without bound.
Offsets are committed from a background thread in _commit_loop, which can race with the consumer's staged offsets or with rebalance callbacks, and can commit for already-revoked partitions.

When an anonymous request and a render-service request use the same namespace, action, resource name, and folder, Service.Check creates the same denial key because both identities use UserUID "0", so an anonymous denial can incorrectly deny the render service even though getRendererPermissions grants wildcard read access; the reverse also contaminates anonymous checks. Include checkReq.IdentityType in the denial key (and delimit or encode fields to prevent tuple collisions).

When two resource identifiers contain underscores, userPermDenialCacheKey maps distinct checks to the same cache entry, so a denial for one resource is returned for another. For example, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") both produce the same key; Grafana UIDs explicitly allow underscore. Encode each component unambiguously (or use a structured/escaped key) before caching denials.

Denial cache can pin a stale denial and defeat the fresh-DB fallback - when Check computes allowed == false, Service.Check stores a denial that later checks return before consulting cached permissions or the database. A user who gains access right after the denial stays denied until the TTL expires.

When GetUserIdentifiers fails while getCachedIdentityPermissions prepares a user cache lookup, Service.Check treats that backend error as a cache miss and calls getIdentityPermissions, which calls GetUserIdentifiers again; a transient identifier-store failure therefore causes two backend requests and can return a different result on the second attempt. Return non-cache errors directly, or distinguish cache.ErrNotFound from identifier lookup failures before falling back.

When a federated rule group reaches useAllRulerRuleAbilities, the hook treats it as mutable because isFederated is hardcoded to false, so users with update/delete permissions can receive pause, update, or delete abilities for rules that must be immutable

Silence drawer never opens for prom-only Grafana rules because the drawer is only mounted when the rule prop is a Grafana ruler alerting rule, but clicking the Silence menu item only sets showSilenceDrawer state
Delete and Pause menu items are unreachable in the list view because AlertRuleMenu gates these items with rulerRule existence check, but GrafanaRuleListItem only provides promRule
FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without a key prop, causing React to use positional reconciliation and potentially reuse stateful row UI for different rules when results reorder
Grafana prom abilities report Duplicate as supported when the rule is skipped because when skipToken is passed, the loading flag is false so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported
When AlertRuleMenu is rendered with only promRule, useRulerRuleAbilities still runs with rulerRule undefined, triggering ruler feature discovery through useIsRuleEditable for every list row

When runShardSplitQuery delegates each shard sub-request to runSplitQuery, runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables again on targets that were already interpolated, causing ad hoc filters to be added twice and selectors to contain duplicate labels or fail Loki parsing

TestLogger.FromContext returns a freshly allocated NewTestLogger() instead of returning the original instance, causing log calls to be recorded on an instance nobody holds, leaving InfoLogs and ErrorLogs on the original fake empty and making assertions on logged messages fail

Race condition in CreateOrUpdateDevice: when two anonymous registrations reach the function concurrently, each call counts below deviceLimit and inserts independently, allowing the anon_device table to grow beyond the configured limit. CountDevices and the later write use separate WithDbSession calls with no transaction or locking across the check-then-insert.

Cache populated before successful store operation: when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, TagDevice propagates the error but tagDeviceUI has already inserted the device's key into localCache, allowing the same device's next authentication to hit the cache and bypass the limit check for up to 29 minutes.

GrafanaBootConfig exposes anonymousDeviceLimit property as type undefined rather than number | undefined, so consumers cannot use the configured limit as a number without narrowing or a cast even though the constructor's merge populates it from boot settings.

Sync tagging on the auth path returns a raw sentinel error: Anonymous.Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request ctx, making every anonymous request with a cache miss wait on a COUNT plus a write before authentication. When the limit is hit, Authenticate returns the bare error.

When the limit is reached and a returning device's existing row is older than the 30-day window, updateDevice's date-bounded update affects no rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, rejecting authentication for a device that is not part of the counted window.

When the limit is reached and a valid existing device is tagged again with the same values, updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached if the driver reports zero changed rows, causing authentication to fail even though the device is already allowed. This occurs on MySQL when the repeated tag falls within the same second because client_ip, user_agent, and the second-precision updated_at are unchanged.

Debug logging at Error level dumps full ID lists on every batch - CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error with full ids slice even on success, polluting error monitoring and inflating log volume

Cleanup ticker interval cut from 10 minutes to 1 minute - CleanUpService.Run ticks every minute instead of every ten, causing cleanup jobs to run 10x as often and potentially causing continuous database cleanup load

When cleanupjob_batchsize exceeds non-SQLite driver's bind-parameter limit (about 65535 on Postgres and MySQL), deleteByIDs builds one placeholder per ID causing DELETE to error and cleanup job to fail on first full batch - need to cap configured batch size or split ID lists into database-safe delete chunks

When the API request finishes or is canceled after unified storage succeeds, Create derives the legacy timeout from the request ctx, so the replication call is already canceled and legacy storage is not updated despite the successful response. Use a detached context that preserves required values (or an explicitly owned background replication context) with the 10-second timeout.

When unified Storage.Create fails, Create records the elapsed storage operation in the legacy histogram, so storage failures are reported under the wrong backend and latency dashboards become misleading. Record this failure with recordStorageDuration; Update has the same wrong helper on its storage-error path.

Legacy DeleteCollection duration recorded as storage duration - when the async legacy DeleteCollection finishes, DeleteCollection records its duration and error with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, causing storage histograms to get spurious samples and legacy histogram to record nothing.

Unguarded dereference of options in the new methods - Get now dereferences options.Kind at lines 65 and 73, so a nil *GetOptions panics where the old code tolerated it. Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection also read options.Kind without a guard, and List reads options.Kind without a guard.

Legacy Update re-runs the caller's objInfo instead of the object written to storage - when unified Storage.Update succeeds, Update passes the original objInfo to d.Legacy.Update in the goroutine, causing legacy to re-run UpdatedObject against its own state rather than receiving the stored result, so the two stores can end up with different content or resource versions.

When a successful Mode 3 test registers asynchronous legacy expectation, the test returns immediately after the unified-store assertion and never calls AssertExpectations or waits for the goroutine, so the test still passes if legacy replication is omitted or never starts.

When mode-3 helper is used, doPlaylistTests immediately performs legacy list/get assertions after Kubernetes creates and updates, but mode 3 schedules those legacy writes in goroutines and provides no completion or polling mechanism, causing legacy assertions to potentially run before replication and fail intermittently.

Legacy write errors are dropped without logging - when d.Legacy.Create, Update, Delete or DeleteCollection fails inside the async goroutines, only a metric label is recorded and the error is never logged, making failed legacy replication hard to diagnose.

When multiple non-development requests enter GetWebAssets during an empty cache, the first caller fills entryPointAssetsCache, but each waiter then proceeds directly to manifest loading because the post-Lock path never rechecks the cache. This serially rereads assets-manifest.json for every concurrent request, causing avoidable startup I/O and latency. Need to recheck the cache after acquiring the write lock before doing any loading.
enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag - the function negates the flag lookup and returns false in both the if enabled branch and the fall-through

SQL disable guard only covers the ReadQuery path - when SQL queries arrive through the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path instead of ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery, the enableSqlExpressions guard is never applied, causing queries to fail with a generic SQL-reading error instead of the 'sqlExpressions is not implemented' error
TotalDocs iterates b.cache without taking cacheMu lock, causing fatal concurrent map iteration/write error when metrics collection runs while BuildIndex updates the cache

BuildIndex no longer serialized per key - concurrent builds can race and replace each other's index because only the final b.cache[key] = idx write is locked, causing file-backed builds to fail on shared directory or memory indexes to silently replace each other losing documents
Per-request Init gate removed so handlers like Create, Read and List no longer call s.Init(ctx), meaning stopped/failed server still serves requests and initErr is never surfaced
When Init fails inside NewResourceServer, it returns without calling the cancel function
When a write occurs after searchSupport.init snapshots resources but before initWatcher subscribes, the search index remains stale and subsequent searches omit that resource

The cleanup is registered against the literal alias "alias", but every provider created by the loop has an alias of "idp-alias-*". Teardown attempts to remove only the nonexistent/wrong provider and leaves all 20 providers in the realm, contaminating later tests and may fail cleanup on a 404. Should capture the generated alias and use it in the deferred lookup.

Update skips login-cache invalidation when original is an org-aware wrapper. When an org-linked public IDP in a disabled organization is updated with hideOnLogin=true, registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate receives a wrapped original that fails the login predicate, returns early because both original and updated fail it, and after the organization is re-enabled the cached login ID set still contains the IDP incorrectly.

readLength() returns -1 for BER indefinite lengths, but neither decoder consumer handles that sentinel. An INTEGER with an indefinite length reaches read(int) with -1 and causes NegativeArraySizeException. Malformed signature input escapes as an unchecked failure instead of being rejected as a parse error. Reject indefinite lengths here (DER does not permit them).

Test fixture leaves EC parameters at provider default (normally P-256), but test invokes ES384 and ES512 as well. Those cases sign with wrong curve and only exercise padding/truncation against P-256 signature, so conversion defects specific to 48-byte or 66-byte R/S values can pass unnoticed. Generate key pair with curve corresponding to each algorithm (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1) instead of sharing default pair.

Tag check compares only low tag-number bits, so it accepts non-universal and non-constructed tags as DER SEQUENCE. A context-specific 0x90 tag has tag number 16 and will pass this test, and its contents are then treated as ECDSA (r,s) sequence. Validate complete expected tag/class/constructed bits before accepting signature.

readNext() is allowed to consume a complete element even when it is larger than the sequence's declared content length; the loop then exits with negative length and returns the element. A sequence whose length field ends in middle of an INTEGER can still be accepted by ECDSA conversion path. Check that each element's encoded length is no greater than remaining sequence content before consuming it.

Oversized DER INTEGERs are truncated instead of rejected. This makes decoder interpret out-of-range r or s modulo 2^(8*qLength), and crafted malformed signature can be transformed into different fixed-width signature value before verification. Reject values whose unsigned magnitude exceeds expected component width rather than dropping high-order bytes.

When signature contains zero-length INTEGER (02 00), readInteger calls new BigInteger(new byte[0]), which throws NumberFormatException. Callers of asn1derToConcatenatedRS that expect IOException for malformed input get runtime exception instead.

readSequence() returns as soon as declared content length has been consumed, without checking that input stream is also exhausted. A valid sequence followed by arbitrary trailing bytes is accepted as signature and converted. Add end-of-input check after parsing the sequence.

readInteger accepts ASN.1 INTEGER encodings as arbitrary signed two's-complement values and does not enforce DER's minimal INTEGER representation. Negative values are sign-extended and oversized values are truncated, so malformed INTEGER encodings can be transformed into different signature value instead of being rejected.

getBouncyCastleProvider does not return a Bouncy Castle provider: it returns whichever provider implements JVM default keystore type (normally SUN for JKS). BouncyIntegration uses this method to set BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER, after which Bouncy-dependent code requests algorithms from that provider by name; those lookups fail or resolve to unrelated implementations.

When several CryptoProvider implementations with equal order() are on classpath, detectProvider picks whichever the sort leaves first and only logs ignored ones at debug level. A default provider could silently win over FIPS in mixed classpath.

Removal listener is gated on the V1 feature flag (ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), which breaks V2 cleanup and V1+V2 client deletion - when V1 is disabled but V2 is enabled, ProviderEventListener skips all role, client and group removal handling, and when both are enabled, ClientRemovedEvent reaches ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled which throws

getClientsWithPermission uses findByType which does not match per-client resources - when a caller holds the requested scope on the all-clients resource, it adds the literal 'Clients' to the granted set instead of client ids, causing callers like available-role-mappings endpoint to resolve a null client and fail

getResourceTypeResource explicitly returns null when the authorization schema/resource is not provisioned, but the result is passed directly to findByResource - when a client has no resource and the Clients type resource is also absent, hasPermission(ClientModel, String) passes null to findByResource causing an exception instead of a denial

A per-client resource hides the all-clients permission - when a client already has its own resource, hasPermission(ClientModel, String) evaluates only that resource and the fallback to all-clients resource only runs when resource == null, so an admin with MANAGE, VIEW or MAP_ROLES on all clients can be denied for a client that has a per-client resource without that scope

ClientPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from isPermissionsEnabled and setPermissionsEnabled when V2 is active and a client calls the client management permissions GET or PUT endpoints, returning a server error instead of a defined response

canView() ignores MANAGE or CONFIGURE on all clients - when an admin holds only an all-clients MANAGE permission, canView() returns false because it only checks canViewClientDefault() and hasPermission(VIEW), denying administrators who can manage all clients

The user search filter expects actual GroupModel IDs, but getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource ID) instead of the group's ID, causing users in permitted groups to be omitted from searches because the IDs never match UserGroupMembershipEntity.groupId

The parameterless canManage() method treats the VIEW scope as sufficient for management by calling hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing administrators with only view permission to pass requireManage() checks and perform group mutations like creating groups

GroupPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled() throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing the group management-permissions endpoint (GET /groups/{id}/management/permissions) to fail with a server error when V2 is enabled instead of returning a response

GroupPermissionsV2.resource() and getPermissions() methods throw UnsupportedOperationException, which are called by the existing group management-permissions endpoint and need V2-safe implementations or the endpoint must be explicitly excluded under V2

The account UI's i18next backend uses {{name}} interpolation syntax, but the message now uses Java MessageFormat placeholders {0}, {1}, and {2,choice,...} which will render as literal text instead of being interpolated
Lithuanian resource messages_lt.properties contains Italian text for totpStep1 instead of Lithuanian translation
Lithuanian login resource messages_lt.properties contains Italian text for loginTotpStep1 instead of Lithuanian translation
Simplified Chinese file messages_zh_CN.properties contains Traditional Chinese text for totpStep1 instead of Simplified Chinese
Diff-position computation in verifySafeHtml can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when sanitized text differs from value only by removed characters that equal their neighbours

santizeAnchors removes every anchor that exactly matches the English value before passing to sanitizer, which bypasses POLICY_SOME_HTML validation for English source files containing unsafe anchors like javascript: hrefs
isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted condition - returns false when items[0].substring(3, 5) equals the expected shortcut instead of returning true
isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offsets (3, 5) when the grant shortcut sits at characters 4-6
The second null check in AccessTokenContext constructor validates grantType again instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to be accepted
When rawTokenId is null, encodeTokenId concatenates it as the literal 'null', producing IDs ending in ':null' that can collide for multiple contexts
ClientCredentialsGrantType.process() does not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE on the ClientSessionContext, so the encoder receives a null grant and the 'cc' shortcut is never used
grantType is cached only in the OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor, but setFormParams() allows replacing request parameters without updating this field, causing stale grant type to be encoded
Federated recovery-code validation only checks membership and never removes the matched code, allowing the same code to be submitted repeatedly and remain valid indefinitely
When the matching credential comes from user storage, removeStoredCredentialById only removes from the local credential store, leaving exhausted federated credentials in user storage

Recovery credentials are reported as configured but disableCredentialType only clears OTP and logs recovery codes as unsupported, leaving myUser.recoveryCodes intact when disabling through credential manager/admin path
Raw recovery codes are sent to user storage in JSON format that createFromCredentialModel cannot parse, causing potential login failures when storage persists the input as given

The test never waits for the reader thread to finish before checking caughtExceptions - the main thread can delete groups, set the flag, and assert while the reader has not yet executed or recorded an exception, so a regression that throws during groups(...) can pass; need to keep a reference to the thread and join() it before asserting

When the backing group is deleted concurrently, GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null because modelSupplier.get() yields null, which violates the non-null contract of GroupModel#getSubGroupsCount - should return zero/empty count instead of null when delegate is absent
The sibling getSubGroupsStream overloads still throw an NPE on the same null delegate when the backing group is deleted concurrently
